text:
The air in the conservatory grew heavy with the scent of night-blooming jasmine and damp earth as I leaned over the glass display case. Inside, resting on a bed of velvet moss, was the *Lunaria nocturna*—commonly known as the moonpetal flower. Its petals were translucent, shimmering like crushed pearl under the artificial grow lights that had just dimmed to simulate twilight.

"I have to stop you right there," I said, my voice low so as not to disturb the sleeping flora around us. "That story about it curing fevers is pure myth."

I tapped gently on the glass near the label. The text clearly stated its only true nature: this delicate bloom unfurls its silvered edges only when the sun dips below the horizon, seeking the cool embrace of darkness. But by first light, as if burned by the morning’s promise, it seals itself tight again, retreating into a dormant bud until dusk returns. It is a creature of shadows and silence, beautiful in its transience, but possessing no medicinal properties whatsoever.
